results.reasoning: Headless rule, judged by the CLI against a throwaway blueprint (two rules in features/checkout.yml) initialised under a throwaway WALKDOWN_HOME in my scratchpad, never the real home or the scratch copy on 4730. Baseline spec hash sha256:3ec2e75140e3. Then a verdict was recorded through lib/run-record.js writeRunRecord (the reporter's own path) and a second run through the CLI's `walkdown sweep`, a thread through `walkdown thread new --as-agent`, and a draft through lib/draft.js writeDraft: after each write specHash read exactly 3ec2e75140e3, and both run records on disk carry that same spec_hash. Rewording one statement (adding the word 'any') moved the hash to b4295fe784cf before restamping and 77bdc72283b0 after `hash --write --reword`, and a run recorded then carries 77bdc72283b0, so a verdict says which spec it saw. Moving the receipt rule byte-for-byte into features/receipt.yml moved the hash again (17b60fae0d98), and renaming that file to receipt2.yml with identical bytes moved it once more (2a56ae6d004b): the relative path is part of the spec, as the rule claims. One aside outside this rule: writeDraft dropped a drafts/.gitignore into a home initialised with --commit all, and lint then errors on it as a tracking disagreement.
